answer: An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the crystal index resolves every citation against the copper checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the summit audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 45 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 45 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 29 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
